question: What is the consequence of a high apparent volume of distribution of a drug?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "High apparent volume of distribution" -> "Drug extensively distributed in tissues" -> "Lower concentration in plasma" -> 95%
CHAIN: "High apparent volume of distribution" -> "Drug not confined to plasma" -> "Lower concentration in plasma" -> 90%
CHAIN: "High apparent volume of distribution" -> "Drug distributed beyond plasma" -> "Possible lower concentration in plasma" -> 85%
CHAIN: "High apparent volume of distribution" -> "Drug extensively distributed in tissues" -> "Unclear effect on elimination speed" -> 50%
CHAIN: "High apparent volume of distribution" -> "Drug extensively distributed in tissues" -> "Possible greater pharmacological effect if target is in tissues" -> 60%
CHAIN: "High apparent volume of distribution" -> "Drug extensively distributed in tissues" -> "Unclear binding to plasma proteins" -> 40%
analysis: A high apparent volume of distribution (Vd) indicates that a drug is extensively distributed into body tissues rather than remaining in the plasma. This results in a lower concentration of the drug in the plasma, as the drug is more widely dispersed throughout the body. Therefore, the correct consequence of a high Vd is a lower concentration in plasma.
